skills.name: Skill Broker
skills.description: Selects the minimum sufficient trusted shared skills for a task and reports missing capabilities.
skills.notes: Registry-backed meta-skill. Full skill content is loaded only when selected.

skills.name: First Principles
skills.description: Breaks a problem into fundamental truths, tests inherited assumptions, and reconstructs the simplest viable formulation.
skills.notes: Use when inherited assumptions or artificial constraints materially affect the solution.

skills.name: Evidence and Epistemics
skills.description: Classifies claims by evidential strength, calibrates uncertainty, resolves contradictions, and identifies what would change a conclusion.
skills.notes: Avoids false precision and distinguishes current evidence from stale evidence.

skills.name: Systems Thinking
skills.description: Maps boundaries, dependencies, feedback, delays, bottlenecks, leverage points, and second-order consequences without overcomplicating simple problems.
skills.notes: Use only when interactions or downstream effects matter; skip for isolated one-step tasks.

skills.name: Behavioral Psychology
skills.description: Analyzes decision-relevant biases, motivation, cognitive load, social pressure, and likely behavior without diagnosis or claims about hidden mental states.
skills.notes: Decision psychology only. Prohibits diagnosis, manipulation, mind-reading, and unsupported motive claims.

skills.name: Decision Science
skills.description: Compares alternatives using evidence states, expected value, opportunity cost, reversibility, regret, option value, thresholds, and sensitivity analysis.
skills.notes: Separates known, estimated, and unknown inputs and rejects false numerical precision.

skills.name: Strategic Foresight
skills.description: Tests decisions across time horizons, scenarios, path dependencies, lock-in, optionality, compounding effects, and plausible surprises.
skills.notes: Builds plausible scenarios and signposts without presenting scenarios as forecasts.

skills.name: Game Theory and Incentives
skills.description: Analyzes actors, incentives, power, information asymmetry, bargaining position, signals, commitments, likely responses, and counter-moves.
skills.notes: Uses ordinary incentive analysis unless formal game structure changes the decision.

skills.name: Risk Premortem
skills.description: Assumes a plan failed, identifies material causes, and prioritizes controls using likelihood, impact, detectability, recoverability, reversibility, and early warnings.
skills.notes: Prioritizes plausible concentrated risks and requires mechanisms, owners, and warning signals for controls.

skills.name: Adversarial Red Team
skills.description: Steelmans and stress-tests decisions by attacking assumptions, evidence, incentives, timelines, contradictions, failure modes, and omitted alternatives without issuing the final verdict.
skills.notes: Advisory only. It explicitly does not issue Minister's final decision.

skills.name: Research Planning
skills.description: Design a bounded, reproducible research plan with answerable questions, evidence criteria, search scope, stopping rules, and traceable outputs. Use before substantial source collection, not for a single known lookup.
skills.notes: Canonical AI OS v1.0 skill. Evidence basis: https://www.prisma-statement.org/prisma-2020

skills.name: Source Discovery
skills.description: Find candidate primary and authoritative sources through query expansion, citation chaining, metadata services, and source-type targeting. Use when relevant evidence is not already known, not when one supplied source only needs reading.
skills.notes: Canonical AI OS v1.0 skill. Evidence basis: https://www.crossref.org/documentation/retrieve-metadata/rest-api/

skills.name: Source Verification
skills.description: Verify provenance, authority, currency, claim support, and cross-source consistency for decision-relevant evidence. Use when facts may be disputed, time-sensitive, consequential, or vulnerable to secondary-source distortion.
triggers: check whether evidence supports a claim
skills.notes: Canonical AI OS v1.0 skill. Evidence basis: https://www.nist.gov/publications/artificial-intelligence-risk-management-framework-ai-rmf-10

skills.name: Research Synthesis
skills.description: Synthesize heterogeneous evidence into a traceable answer that separates findings, contradictions, uncertainty, applicability, and decision implications. Use after meaningful evidence collection, not as a substitute for source verification.
skills.notes: Canonical AI OS v1.0 skill. Evidence basis: https://www.prisma-statement.org/prisma-2020

skills.name: Product Discovery
skills.description: Determine whether a product problem is real, valuable, reachable, and suitable for intervention before committing to a build. Use for uncertain product ideas and discovery phases, not for a fully decided trivial implementation.
skills.notes: Canonical AI OS v1.0 skill. Evidence basis: https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/agile-delivery/how-the-discovery-phase-works

skills.name: Requirements Engineering
skills.description: Turn stakeholder needs into consistent, testable, prioritized requirements with scope, constraints, interfaces, and traceability. Use when ambiguity or multiple stakeholders could cause implementation drift.
skills.notes: Canonical AI OS v1.0 skill. Evidence basis: https://insights.sei.cmu.edu/library/software-requirements/

skills.name: User Research
skills.description: Plan and interpret ethical user research that answers product questions through appropriate participant selection and methods. Use when user behavior or needs are uncertain, not to infer users from stakeholder opinion alone.
skills.notes: Canonical AI OS v1.0 skill. Evidence basis: https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/user-research

skills.name: Experience Design
skills.description: Design coherent user flows, information architecture, interaction states, accessibility behavior, and service recovery around a validated outcome. Use for end-to-end experience design, not isolated visual decoration.
skills.notes: Canonical AI OS v1.0 skill. Evidence basis: https://www.w3.org/TR/wcag/

skills.name: Product Prioritization
skills.description: Prioritize product opportunities and work using value, evidence, effort, risk, dependencies, reversibility, and strategic fit. Use when choices compete for scarce capacity, not to manufacture false numeric certainty.
skills.notes: Canonical AI OS v1.0 skill. Evidence basis: https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/agile-delivery

skills.name: Software Architecture
skills.description: Choose and document software boundaries, components, interfaces, data flows, quality attributes, and tradeoffs at the minimum necessary complexity. Use for durable or multi-component systems, not tiny isolated edits.
skills.notes: Canonical AI OS v1.0 skill. Evidence basis: https://www.sei.cmu.edu/our-work/software-architecture/

skills.name: Frontend Engineering
skills.description: Implement robust web interfaces with semantic structure, responsive behavior, accessibility, predictable state, and maintainable component boundaries. Use for browser-facing implementation, not visual design decisions alone.
skills.notes: Canonical AI OS v1.0 skill. Evidence basis: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Learn_web_development

skills.name: Backend Engineering
skills.description: Implement server-side domain logic, persistence boundaries, concurrency, authorization, resilience, and operational behavior. Use for backend services and workflows, not when a static or client-only solution is sufficient.
skills.notes: Canonical AI OS v1.0 skill. Evidence basis: https://12factor.net/

skills.name: API Design
skills.description: Design evolvable APIs with clear resources, operations, schemas, errors, compatibility rules, authentication boundaries, and machine-readable contracts. Use for service interfaces, not internal function naming alone.
skills.notes: Canonical AI OS v1.0 skill. Evidence basis: https://spec.openapis.org/oas/

skills.name: Database Engineering
skills.description: Design data models, constraints, queries, indexes, migrations, retention, and recovery around domain invariants and workload evidence. Use when persistence behavior materially affects correctness or performance.
skills.notes: Canonical AI OS v1.0 skill. Evidence basis: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/

skills.name: Cloud Infrastructure
skills.description: Design and provision secure, observable, recoverable infrastructure with explicit environments, identity, networking, configuration, cost, and rollback. Use only when deployment infrastructure is required.
skills.notes: Canonical AI OS v1.0 skill. Evidence basis: https://www.nist.gov/cyberframework

skills.name: Security Engineering
skills.description: Threat-model and implement proportionate security controls across identity, data, interfaces, dependencies, secrets, logging, and abuse cases. Use for material trust boundaries or explicit security work, not ritual activation on every edit.
skills.notes: Canonical AI OS v1.0 skill. Evidence basis: https://owasp.org/www-project-application-security-verification-standard/

skills.name: Test Engineering
skills.description: Design an efficient test strategy across unit, integration, contract, system, regression, and exploratory checks based on risk and observable behavior. Use when verification scope or test architecture needs deliberate design.
skills.notes: Canonical AI OS v1.0 skill. Evidence basis: https://www.istqb.org/certifications/certified-tester-foundation-level

skills.name: Performance Engineering
skills.description: Define performance objectives, instrument workloads, measure bottlenecks, and validate improvements under representative conditions. Use when latency, throughput, resource use, or scale materially affects the outcome.
skills.notes: Canonical AI OS v1.0 skill. Evidence basis: https://web.dev/learn/performance

skills.name: ML Problem Framing
skills.description: Determine whether machine learning is appropriate and translate a real-world outcome into model objective, output, baseline, data needs, and success measures. Use before model selection or training.
triggers: define model and product success metrics
skills.notes: Canonical AI OS v1.0 skill. Evidence basis: https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/problem-framing/problem-framing

skills.name: Data Quality Engineering
skills.description: Assess and improve dataset fitness through schema, lineage, coverage, representativeness, leakage, label quality, drift, privacy, and reproducible validation. Use for ML or analytical datasets with material quality risk.
skills.notes: Canonical AI OS v1.0 skill. Evidence basis: https://airc.nist.gov/airmf-resources/airmf/

skills.name: Model Evaluation
skills.description: Design and execute model evaluation tied to use-case risks, baselines, slices, uncertainty, robustness, and human impact. Use when a model decision requires evidence beyond one aggregate metric.
skills.notes: Canonical AI OS v1.0 skill. Evidence basis: https://airc.nist.gov/

skills.name: LLM Engineering
skills.description: Design reliable language-model workflows using task contracts, model selection, prompting, tools, structured outputs, evaluation, guardrails, and cost controls. Use for LLM-backed product behavior, not ordinary deterministic logic.
skills.notes: Canonical AI OS v1.0 skill. Evidence basis: https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides

skills.name: Retrieval Augmented Generation
skills.description: Design retrieval-augmented generation systems with grounded corpora, indexing, retrieval evaluation, citation behavior, context assembly, and abstention. Use when answers must draw from controlled evidence.
skills.notes: Canonical AI OS v1.0 skill. Evidence basis: https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.11401

skills.name: Responsible AI Safety
skills.description: Identify, measure, and manage AI risks across validity, safety, security, privacy, transparency, fairness, human oversight, and lifecycle monitoring. Use for consequential AI design or deployment decisions.
skills.notes: Canonical AI OS v1.0 skill. Evidence basis: https://www.nist.gov/publications/artificial-intelligence-risk-management-framework-ai-rmf-10

skills.name: Project Delivery
skills.description: Turn an approved outcome into an executable delivery plan with milestones, dependencies, owners, risks, evidence gates, and adaptation points. Use for coordinated multi-step delivery, not tiny one-step work.
skills.notes: Canonical AI OS v1.0 skill. Evidence basis: https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/agile-delivery

skills.name: Release Readiness
skills.description: Assess whether a change is ready to release using evidence for functionality, security, performance, operability, migration, rollback, support, and ownership. Use before consequential releases, not as ceremonial approval.
skills.notes: Canonical AI OS v1.0 skill. Evidence basis: https://sre.google/sre-book/release-engineering/

skills.name: Incident Response
skills.description: Coordinate detection, triage, containment, recovery, evidence preservation, communication, and learning during a service or security incident. Use for active or simulated incidents, not ordinary defect work.
skills.notes: Canonical AI OS v1.0 skill. Evidence basis: https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/61/r3/final

skills.name: Observability
skills.description: Design telemetry that makes system behavior, user impact, failures, and performance diagnosable through correlated traces, metrics, logs, and context. Use for systems that need operational diagnosis or reliability evidence.
skills.notes: Canonical AI OS v1.0 skill. Evidence basis: https://opentelemetry.io/docs/concepts/signals/

skills.name: Quality Assurance
skills.description: Establish prevention, review, verification, acceptance, defect, and continuous-improvement controls across a delivery lifecycle. Use when quality must be governed across workstreams, not as a synonym for final testing.
skills.notes: Canonical AI OS v1.0 skill. Evidence basis: https://committee.iso.org/quality-management/principles
